historyOfPresentIllness.incidentNarrative: The patient reports persistent low back pain after lifting a heavy box at work on 12/18/2024.
historyOfPresentIllness.caseWideSummary: The patient sustained a low back injury on 12/18/2024 after lifting a heavy box at work, resulting in low back pain radiating into the right leg. An initial orthopedic evaluation by Dr. Maya Chen on 01/08/2025 diagnosed a lumbar disc herniation with right-sided radicular symptoms, prescribing Naproxen, ordering an MRI, and referring for physical therapy. An MRI of the lumbar spine on 01/20/2025 confirmed a right paracentral L4-5 disc extrusion contacting the traversing right L5 nerve root. The patient began physical therapy at Northside Physical Therapy, with a progress note on 02/14/2025 indicating pain improvement from 7/10 to 4/10, though prolonged sitting and lifting remain difficult. Objective findings showed improved lumbar flexion but a persistent positive right straight-leg raise. The patient continues with physical therapy and is on modified duty with restrictions, as documented in a work status report on 03/10/2025.

impression: Right paracentral L4-5 disc extrusion contacting the traversing right L5 nerve root.

patient_subjective_trajectory.interpretation: Patient-reported pain improved from 7/10 to 4/10 by 2025-02-14. However, there is no subjective pain report for today's examination (2026-10-16), leaving the current subjective status and long-term trajectory uncertain.

patient_objective_trajectory.interpretation: Lumbar flexion improved from 45 degrees (2025-01-08) to 60 degrees (2025-02-14), and right straight-leg raise improved from 50 to 60 degrees. However, today's examination (2026-10-16) presents new objective findings of left L4 radiculopathy (loss of sharp/dull discrimination, positive femoral nerve stretch), which is discordant with the initial right-sided symptoms and MRI findings of right L5 nerve root involvement. No current lumbar ROM or straight-leg raise findings are provided for comparison.

patient_functional_trajectory.interpretation: Initial functional improvements included increased sitting tolerance from 30 to 45 minutes (by 2025-02-14) and increased lifting capacity from 15 to 20 lbs (by 2025-03-10), though new restrictions were also added. Today's PDQ (2026-10-16) indicates persistent moderate functional limitations across various activities (e.g., lifting low 4/10, sit/stand 4/10, walk/run 5/10), suggesting a stable level of functional impairment after initial changes.
